summary: We developed a web page that provides safety information for astronauts looking to traverse through mars, specifically routes covered by the curiosity rover. This addresses the challenge as it helps astronauts preview courses ahead and gain knowledge about the region they are currently in. Which is important as it lets them see any areas to caution due to its elevation, UV radiation, temperature, and visibility.
details: Our project, MarshWalk is an interactive map designed to help astronauts traverse and explore mars for scientific purposes. The map itself is divided into segments for easier navigation. Our main goal is to ensure our astronauts' safety. We also include a safety score which provides a score of safety dependent on the conditions of mars such as temperature, visibility, terrain, and weather conditions. The web page displays hazards and science goals based on the location and coordinates of the astronauts position. The benefit of MarshWalk is the easy to follow map, detailed information based on location, and safety. The intended impact is to keep the astronauts safe and informed as they explore mars scientifically. We developed MarshWalk using VSCode, Github, CSS, HTML, Javascript, and data provided by NASA. For our data we used multiple resources and NASA data and compiled it into a google sheet, organizing our data based on multiple factors and terrain to provide the best data analysis possible from the curiosity rover. We first took inspiration from Spiderman: Brand New Day, and its spidey tracker, and built our own MarshWalk from that idea. Our team prioritized safety as the main aspect of our project and considered all factors that would contribute to that. We imagined ourselves as astronauts on Mars and envisioned what we would want on our Martian Map.
